issues.legal_issue: A court cannot convert a suit for declaration of title and injunction into a suit for partition and grant partition as a lesser relief when the causes of action differ and the suit omits other joint family properties and co-sharers.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought suits seeking declaration of title and permanent injunction over land, claiming it had been allotted to him in a family partition.
The defendants claimed that the land was joint family property and had been allotted to the first defendants in a later partition.
The first appellate court found that a partition had occurred but that the evidence did not establish that the suit land was allotted to the first defendants.
On amendment applications in the second appeals, the High Court granted a preliminary decree for a one-third share, although the suits did not include all joint family properties or all co-sharers.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in granting partition through amendment; the trial court’s and first appellate court’s decrees dismissing the suits were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not make an amendment appropriate merely because it is sought. A suit for declaration and injunction and a suit for partition involve different causes of action and reliefs; a partial partition is not maintainable when other joint family properties are omitted and the other co-sharers are not impleaded. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: civil_suit_for_declaration_and_injunction and amendment_seeks_partition and other_joint_family_properties_omitted and co_sharers_not_joined

predicates.civil_suit_for_declaration_and_injunctio: A plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking a declaration of title and an injunction.
predicates.amendment_seeks_partition: The plaintiff sought to amend the suit to obtain partition.
predicates.other_joint_family_properties_omitted: The suit did not include all of the joint family properties.
predicates.co_sharers_not_joined: The suit did not include all of the co-sharers as parties.
predicates.partition_decree_not_granted: The court does not grant a decree for partition in the suit.

issues.definition: When a declaration-and-injunction suit is amended to seek partition but omits other joint family properties and co-sharers, the output is that a partition decree is not granted.

issues.legal_issue: When a defendant dies during an appeal and the defendant’s legal representatives are not brought on record, the appeal abates as to that defendant and the trial finding in that defendant’s favour becomes final and binding.
material_facts: A first defendant died while the first appeal was pending.
The first defendant’s legal representatives were not brought on record, and the defendant’s name was deleted from the array of parties.
The trial court had found that the suit property was allotted to that defendant in a partition.
The High Court treated the cause of action as surviving against the other defendant and granted partition, despite the abatement.
issues.conclusion: The suit had abated as against the deceased first defendant; the trial finding in that defendant’s favour had become final and binding, and it was incorrect to hold that the cause of action survived against the other defendant.
issues.legal_principle: The judgment holds that failure to bring a deceased defendant’s legal representatives on record during the appeal results in abatement as to that defendant; the trial finding in that defendant’s favour then remains final and binding between the parties. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited for this point.

rule.if: first_appeal_in_civil_suit and defendant_died_during_appeal and legal_representatives_not_substituted and deceased_defendant_removed_from_case and trial_finding_favored_deceased_defendant

predicates.first_appeal_in_civil_suit: A first appeal in a civil suit was pending.
predicates.defendant_died_during_appeal: A defendant died while the first appeal was pending.
predicates.legal_representatives_not_substituted: The deceased defendant’s legal representatives were not brought on record.
predicates.deceased_defendant_removed_from_case: The deceased defendant’s name was deleted from the case.
predicates.trial_finding_favored_deceased_defendant: The trial court made a finding in favour of the deceased defendant.
predicates.appeal_abates_as_to_deceased_defendant_a: The appeal abates as to the deceased defendant and the trial finding in that defendant’s favour remains final and binding.

issues.definition: When a defendant dies during a first appeal, the legal representatives are not substituted, the defendant is removed from the case, and the trial finding favoured that defendant, the appeal abates as to that defendant and the finding remains final.
